title: CAT Stock Alert: Caterpillar's AI Infrastructure Boom Is Just Getting Started
excerpt: Caterpillar’s record quarter shows how the AI data-center buildout is boosting demand for its power-generation and construction equipment.
content_html:
Caterpillar (CAT) just gave investors another reason to take its AI infrastructure story seriously. The industrial giant delivered a record second quarter, with revenue topping $20 billion for the first time as demand for construction equipment and power-generation products surged. Data centers are becoming a meaningful part of that growth story.

Caterpillar reported revenue growth of 24% year-over-year (YoY), while adjusted earnings reached $8.17 per share. That was far above Wall Street expectations. The company also raised its full-year sales growth outlook to the mid-to-high teens.

The bigger takeaway is that Caterpillar is benefiting from the AI boom without selling a single GPU. Its equipment is helping build and power the infrastructure behind data centers.

CAT Stock Has Had a Huge Run

CAT stock has been one of the market's biggest industrial winners in 2026. Shares are up roughly 51% year-to-date (YTD), even after falling more than 19% from their June peak. Over the past year, the stock has gained more than 100%. 

The rally has been fueled by strong construction demand, AI-related power spending, and a record backlog. The recent pullback reflected valuation worries and concerns about data center regulations. Today's earnings beat, however, shows that demand remains powerful.

There is a catch. CAT is expensive by traditional industrial stock standards.

Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) is around 36 times, compared with roughly 26 times for the broader industrial sector. Its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio is also around 6 times, well above the machinery industry's roughly 1.5 times median. Investors are clearly paying a premium for Caterpillar's stronger growth and AI exposure. 

That premium can work if earnings keep accelerating. It can also become a problem if growth slows.

Data Centers Are Becoming a Major Growth Engine

The latest quarter showed why investors are increasingly treating Caterpillar as an AI infrastructure play.

Power and Energy revenue jumped 17% to $8.24 billion. Construction Industries revenue surged 35% to $8.35 billion. Resource Industries added another 20% to reach $4.65 billion. Together, Power and Energy and Construction Industries accounted for more than 80% of total revenue.

content_html_zh:
卡特彼勒（CAT）刚刚给了投资者另一个认真对待其人工智能基础设施故事的理由。 随着建筑设备和发电产品需求激增，这家工业巨头第二季度营收首次突破 200 亿美元，创下历史新高。 数据中心正在成为这一增长故事中有意义的一部分。

卡特彼勒报告收入同比增长 24%，调整后每股收益达到 8.17 美元。 这远高于华尔街的预期。 该公司还将全年销售增长预期上调至中高位。

  • 美光科技股价下跌 31%，但华尔街支持 MU 股票
  • 西部数据和闪迪的业绩指引令人失望，纳斯达克期货下跌

更大的收获是，Caterpillar 无需出售任何 GPU，就能从人工智能热潮中受益。 其设备正在帮助构建数据中心背后的基础设施并为其提供动力。

CAT 股票大幅上涨

CAT 股票是 2026 年市场最大的工业赢家之一。 尽管较 6 月份的峰值下跌了 19% 以上，但该股今年迄今仍上涨了约 51%。 过去一年，该股涨幅超过100%。

强劲的建筑需求、人工智能相关的电力支出以及创纪录的积压推动了这一涨势。 最近的回调反映了估值担忧和对数据中心监管的担忧。 然而，今天的盈利好转表明需求仍然强劲。

有一个问题。 按照传统工业库存标准，CAT 价格昂贵。

其远期市盈率 (P/E) 约为 36 倍，而更广泛的工业部门约为 26 倍。 其市销率 (P/S) 也在 6 倍左右，远高于机械行业大约 1.5 倍的中位数。 投资者显然为卡特彼勒强劲的增长和人工智能业务付出了溢价。

如果盈利持续加速，这种溢价就可以发挥作用。 如果增长放缓，它也可能成为一个问题。

数据中心正在成为主要的增长引擎

最新季度显示了为什么投资者越来越多地将卡特彼勒视为人工智能基础设施公司。

电力和能源收入增长 17%，达到 82.4 亿美元。 建筑行业收入猛增 35%，达到 83.5 亿美元。 资源行业又增加了 20%，达到 46.5 亿美元。 电力能源和建筑行业合计占总收入的80%以上。
